key_insight: Strict causal light cones bound the Fourier bandwidth of shared-parameter energy slices, enabling exact quantum optimization gradients from fewer circuit settings.
engineering_relevance: For QAOA at fixed depth on bounded-degree graphs, the circuit settings needed for a cost-angle derivative drop from O(m) to O(1), where m is the number of interaction terms.
method: Use commuting local layer generators and Heisenberg light cones to bound frequency bandwidth.
Recover exact derivatives with a discrete-sine-transform multipoint parameter-shift rule when frequencies lie on a known lattice.
For QAOA cost angles, determine the relevant geometry through contact regions in the interaction line graph.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical circuit-setting reduction for QAOA, but provides no numerical benchmarks or hardware evaluation.
watch_item: The O(1) setting count assumes fixed depth and bounded degree; it does not establish constant shot cost or noise-free gradients on hardware.
paper_title: Strict Frequency Bandwidths from Causal Light Cones Enable Scalable Exact Gradient Evaluation in Quantum Optimization
